subject.title: feat(browser): side panel copilot with per-tab agent sessions

question: Should the bundled browser panel ship only after browser actions are runtime-bound to its pinned shared tab, or is prompt-only URL/title targeting an accepted product contract?
rationale: The current patch is functional in a one-tab demonstration, but choosing whether model text may select among consented tabs defines a user-intent and security boundary that automation cannot safely settle.

options.title: Require trusted tab binding
options.body: Add a typed relay/gateway target context enforced by the browser tool and validate it with a multi-tab real-browser scenario before merge.

options.title: Accept prompt-only targeting
options.body: Document that the panel isolates conversation history but browser actions may select any shared tab, explicitly owning the wrong-tab risk.

options.title: Keep it external for now
options.body: Publish the panel as a plugin or external extension until core exposes a narrow trusted tab-targeting API.

recommendation.title: Require trusted tab binding
recommendation.body: Add a typed relay/gateway target context enforced by the browser tool and validate it with a multi-tab real-browser scenario before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: The merged extension relay and its tab-group consent model originated in this person's current-main work, making them the clearest owner of whether the boundary may expand.
